source.publisher: Derry Journal (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: image-read: DJ 8 Jan 1923 (INA block 3): for the South Ward 'Prima-facie Alderman Bonner, Councillors Bradley, Cosgrove, Con Doherty, Gallagher, and M'Ananey would be deemed to be re-elected, leaving two vacancies to be filled'; Londonderry Sentinel 11 Jan 1923 p5 (BNA article image): 'the six representatives of the South-East Ward will be deemed to be re-elected for the South Ward. This would still leave two vacancies'; DJ 22 Jan 1923 p4 (BNA crops): 'The fourteen Nationalist members of the old Corporation for the South and West Wards have been summoned' to the quarterly meeting, with the Town Clerk's form declaring 'the aldermen and councillors of the South Ward deemed to be re-elected', and Alderman Bonner named as deemed re-elected for the South. Irish News 11 Jan 1923 p5 (OCR, finding aid): the notice 'concerns fourteen members, leaving still two seats to be filled'.

note: First election of the whole Corporation on the restored five wards (nominations closed Friday 5 January 1923). No one was nominated for the South or West Ward; the Returning Officer (F. Henry Miller) gave notice that the retiring aldermen and councillors for those wards would be declared to be deemed re-elected. The notices went to fourteen Nationalist members of the old Corporation: the eight West Ward members and the six Nationalists of the old South-East (PR) area for the South Ward, which has eight seats, so two South Ward seats were left unfilled. Deemed re-elected (no nomination) under r.10 of the county borough election order; first names from the January 1920 South-East return (James Bonner, W. J. Bradley, Michael Cosgrove, Con Doherty, James Gallagher, Robert M'Ananey), as for the West Ward. Bonner is printed as alderman, the others as councillors. Two of the ward's eight seats were left without a member: the old South-East area's other alderman, H. Babington, now sat for the East Ward. The Derry Journal (8 January) said the six would refuse the declaration; none of the deemed-re-elected Nationalists attended the first meeting of 23 January 1923 (Belfast News-Letter, 24 January 1923, p. 8). Whether their seats were later declared vacant is not recorded here. Entered with six seats, the number filled: the ward elected eight members, and two seats were left without a member.
